issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Mesh: Fw Distribution Server issues with OOB upload
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
There are few issues with OOB upload in Fw Distribution Server that were caught by PTS:
1. Fw Distribution Server is unable to receive Upload OOB Start message due to incorrect check of the message length: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/47822586e41a76d834e4432c2bcc75ab17fcfaca/subsys/bluetooth/mesh/dfd_srv.c#L746 It uses `BT_MESH_LEN_EXACT` while should have been `BT_MESH_LEN_MIN`.
2. When receiving Upload OOB Start message after failed upload started by Upload Start message, the Fw Distribution server doesn't release the already reserved slot which make the server to fail processing the message once it runs out of available slots.
3. If another Upload OOB Start message is received before the Check Firmware OOB procedure is completed (`bt_mesh_dfd_srv_oob_check_complete()` wasn't called yet), the Fw Distribution server will process this message again which will result in an invalid state in server.
4. When the Check Firmware OOB procedure is completed (a user called `bt_mesh_dfd_srv_oob_check_complete()`) and the firmware was already received, the server will call `oob_progress_get` callback to get the progress from a user application. But the user application doesn't know yet that the firmware is already received. This will happen after `bt_mesh_dfd_srv_oob_check_complete()` returns status. Thus, the server returns wrong progress when sends status to the Fw Distribution client.

**To Reproduce**
Affected tests:
- DFU/SR/FD/BV-06-C
- DFU/SR/FD/BV-13-C
- DFU/SR/FD/BV-14-C
- DFU/SR/FD/BV-15-C
- DFU/SR/FD/BV-16-C
- DFU/SR/FD/BV-17-C
- DFU/SR/FD/BV-18-C
- DFU/SR/FD/BV-22-C

**Impact**
Qualification of Mesh DFU v1.0.0.

review_comments:
I guess commit message mistyping. It should be `This message _at least_ 2 bytes long, but can be longer, thus
BT_MESH_LEN_EXACT shouldn't be used.` or `This message _at least_ 2 bytes long, but can be longer, thus
BT_MESH_LEN_MIN should be used.`

Shouldn't it be `https`?
http commands are used but seems URI has https scheme (at least in 3.2.1 Construction of the Request URI)
Then we need to support Firmware Check Over HTTPS and Firmware Retrieval over HTTPS procedures according to sections 6.2.2.2 and 6.2.2.3. But we don't support them.
This situation will unlikely happen. They are not scheduled with delay.
Should this be >= or <=, or is it correct with exact 99. dfd_srv_oob_ctx.progress can be less than 99.
ASFAIK The image is ready for storing if progress is exactly 99. After storing it will be 100.
No, `MIN` will not let it to be set greater than 99.
